literal: She who wears a garland and small bracelets gave [me] the grief that afflicts [me] in the evening, along with [the need to ride] the palmyra-stem horse.
translation: She who wears a flower garland and small bracelets has given me this grief, which afflicts me in the evening, along with the desperate urge to ride the palmyra-stem horse.
modern: மாலை போன்ற மாலையையும் சிறிய வளையல்களையும் அணிந்தவள், எனக்கு மாலைப் பொழுதில் வருத்தும் துன்பத்தையும், அதனுடன் மடல் ஏறும் நிலையையும் தந்துவிட்டாள்.
explanation: In this verse, the hero expresses his intense suffering due to separation from his beloved. He describes her as one wearing a flower garland (தொடலை) and small bracelets (குறுந்தொடி). He laments that she has given him a deep grief (துயர்) that torments him especially during the evening (மாலை). This unbearable sorrow drives him to the extreme step of riding the 'maḍal' (மடல்), a traditional practice where a desperate lover publicly rides a horse made of rough palmyra stems to proclaim his love.
